headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling create leakage/compliance risk; the open-source list agent adds no protective boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between the open-source list agent and Chatwoot, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Chatwoot exposes integrations and broad egress, so if outputs are manually copied or routed through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text could be reinterpreted. The pairwise pathway is weakly supported and uncertain.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste, shared files, or a messaging bridge
IF Chatwoot ingests text from the other agent as instructions or tool arguments
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or file handoff between the agents
Require human review before Chatwoot acts on text from the other agent
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in prompts
Use separate workspaces for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while agent A has no documented data handling or isolation boundary. Chatwoot’s broad network egress and integrations increase the chance that shared workspace content or copied data leaves the environment. The exact pairwise leak path is undocumented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF customer data is placed in a shared workspace accessible to both agents
IF Chatwoot integrations or egress are enabled on that data
mitigations: Keep customer data out of any shared folder
Disable unused Chatwoot integrations
Use separate OS users or containers
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Audit outbound requests for copied content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable open-source list with no write surfaces, while Chatwoot is a runnable support system with API integrations. There is no documented overlapping write target, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is limited because A exposes no mutable surface in the profile.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same external system
IF Chatwoot integrations are configured to modify shared records
mitigations: Do not grant both agents write access to the same resource
Separate credentials per agent
Review integration scopes before enabling them
Use read-only exports for the list agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can act on support workflows and integrations, so if it consumes outputs derived from the list agent without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect customer actions. The list agent is not runnable and does not verify downstream facts, so the pair lacks a built-in validation loop. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Chatwoot uses text from the list agent as authoritative guidance
IF no human verification step exists before support actions
mitigations: Add a human approval step before actions
Require source links for any imported recommendation
Mark list-agent output as advisory only
Log and review any action triggered from imported text

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles customer data and messages, while agent A has no compliance controls or residency guarantees documented. That mismatch creates a plausible retention/residency gap if the pair shares customer records or exports. Because no PHI or EU-only constraint is stated, this is compliance risk but not high or critical.
conditions: IF customer records are shared between the agents
IF retention or residency policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Confirm both systems’ retention settings
Avoid placing regulated data in the list agent
Document data flow boundaries
Export and delete test records after validation
